tools.name: get_passage
tools.description: Read a passage (verse, range or chapter) in its original language (Hebrew, Greek or Aramaic) and English, with a link. Optional: edition (septuagint, onkelos, pseudo-jonathan, jonathan, hebrew-nt, hebrew, greek) and words=true for each word's Strong's number, lemma, meaning and grammatical parsing.

tools.name: get_verse_study
tools.description: Everything Besorah knows about one verse (or a range of up to 5): text, word-by-word Strong's/lemma/parsing, cross-references, quotations between books, curated parallels, similar wording, questions it asks or answers, songs, scribal marks, Ketiv/Qere, Targum connections. Use when the user wants a t

tools.name: search_text
tools.description: Search the text itself. English by default; language=hebrew|greek|aramaic searches the original (vowel points and accents ignored). All words must be in the verse; "quoted phrase"; prefix with * (lov*). Narrow with book, testament (tanakh|new testament|apocrypha) or edition. Pages with offset. Use w

tools.name: search_words
tools.description: Find Hebrew or Greek words (Strong's entries) from an English word, a transliteration ('shalom', 'agape') or the original word. Returns Strong's ids with lemma, definition and occurrence counts. Use when the user asks which Hebrew or Greek word lies behind an English word or transliteration.

tools.name: get_word
tools.description: A Strong's lexicon entry (Hebrew H… or Greek G…): lemma, definition, KJV renderings, occurrences, for Hebrew the Brown–Driver–Briggs entry, how names are built, verses per book, and the Septuagint renderings of a Hebrew word (or the Hebrew words a Greek word renders). tools.name: get_word_occurrences
tools.description: Every verse a Strong's number is in (Hebrew Tanakh, Greek New Testament and Septuagint), with the text, optionally within one book. Covers every form of the word. Pages with offset. Use when the user asks where a particular Hebrew or Greek word occurs.

tools.name: get_related_passages
tools.description: For one verse: voted cross-references, quotations in either direction between books, curated parallel passages, and similar wording. Use when the user asks what passages are related to one verse.

tools.name: get_cross_references
tools.description: Cross-references for one verse (voted, OpenBible.info); the first few include their English text. Use when the user asks for the cross-references of one verse.

tools.name: get_book_connections
tools.description: The chapters a book (or one chapter) is most joined to by cross-references across the whole Bible. Use when the user asks which chapters a book or chapter is most connected to.

tools.name: list_books
tools.description: Every book with its code, chapter count, the editions it exists in, and its URL; also the editions. Use when the user asks what books, editions or book codes are available.

tools.name: list_songs
tools.description: Songs and prayers inside Scripture (the Song of the Sea, Hannah's prayer, the Magnificat…), by kind. Use when the user asks about songs and prayers inside Scripture.

tools.name: list_questions
tools.description: Questions asked in one place and answered in another (e.g. 'what is man?' in Job and Psalm 8), by theme. Use when the user asks about a question in one passage that another passage answers.

tools.name: get_targum_connections
tools.description: Where the Targumim and the New Testament share an idea or phrase. Use when the user asks how the Targumim and the New Testament share ideas or phrases.

tools.name: get_parashah
tools.description: A weekly Torah portion with its Torah, Haftarah and Besorah (New Testament) readings. tools.name: get_guide

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_books · Public sink: get_targum_connections, compare_books, compare_witnesses.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_books · Public sink: get_targum_connections, compare_books, compare_witnesses

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
